newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks need consensus to lower inflation - IMF/Hardy.
newsitem.headline: Turks need consensus to lower inflation - IMF/Hardy.

text.p: A senior International Monetary Fund (IMF) figure said on Thursday that Turkey needed political consensus to lower chronic inflation and urged the government to implement an anti-inflation programme.

"Turkey faces chronic inflation for many years but has been unable to create a political consensus to solve this serious prblem," Martin Hardy, the IMF Assistant Director to Europe, told a Euromoney conference in Istanbul which ended on Thursday.
Hardy, who also heads the IMF Turkey desk, said although chronic inflation was something that Turks had become accustomed to living with, it had a serious and negative impact on the economy.
"Our advice to the government is to detail its medium-term programme to tackle chronic inflation. They must work with coordination and insist on realising this target," he said.
Turkey's annual consumer inflation stood at 77.2 percent in April, compared with 77.3 percent in the same period in 1996.
Hardy said Turkey had showed some economic improvement in recent years, with higher growth, but saw weakness in public finances as one of the country's major problems.
